message:
fix(release): the staging layout, and a manifest that verified while being wrong

Three corrections, and the middle one is the interesting failure.

The staged ui/ files were flat while the manifest points at .../ui/shell.html
and .../ui/macro.html. The bytes were right and only the location was wrong,
so publishing it would have delivered seven executables and 404'd the last
two -- failing mid-download, and looking like a server fault.

Fixing that meant rebuilding the APK, and I signed the manifest without
regenerating it. Every check passed: the C++ verifier, the Node verifier,
the self-check after signing. They were all correct and all beside the
point. A signature says the document has not changed since it was signed. It
says nothing about whether the document describes files that exist, and the
manifest was naming a size and a hash nothing on disk had.

So there is now a check that reads every artifact line back and compares it
against the staged file -- ten of ten -- and the handoff says plainly that
signature verification does not stand in for it.

Third: the 328,312-byte difference between the two APKs, which "only the
version changed" could not explain. Every entry had the same uncompressed
size, the same compressed size, the same compression method; the signing
block and central directory matched. The difference was dead space between
classes2.dex and the first native library, left by an incremental build and
belonging to no entry. Valid APK, valid signature, and an artifact carrying
bytes nobody could account for -- so both were rebuilt clean. They are now
the same size, with two entries differing and 118 matching by CRC.

A number that does not add up is usually a fact that has not been named yet.
